subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should an in-run model be allowed to request compaction of its own active session through `session_status`?
rationale: This adds a model-controlled mutation that interrupts the current run and changes session state; source inspection can validate the implementation shape, but only maintainers can set the intended trust and operator-control boundary.

options.title: Allow current-session only
options.body: Approve the narrow direct PR after branch refresh, retaining current-session checks, fail-closed unsupported contexts, and existing recovery semantics.

options.title: Require an operator gate
options.body: Keep the implementation but expose self-compaction only through an explicit approved tool-policy or configuration gate.

options.title: Keep external control only
options.body: Decline a model-callable mutation and retain automatic, manual sender-authorized, and administrative compaction paths.

recommendation.title: Allow current-session only
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow direct PR after branch refresh, retaining current-session checks, fail-closed unsupported contexts, and existing recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail most strongly connects this person to both the original status tool and the current session/compaction product boundary.
